title: Merge Strings Alternately
scenario:
You get two strings, word1 and word2. Merge them by taking letters in turn — first from word1, then from word2, and so on. If one word is longer, add its remaining letters at the end. Return the merged string.

Example 1:
Input: word1 = "abc", word2 = "pqr"
Output: "apbqcr"

Example 2:
Input: word1 = "ab", word2 = "pqrs"
Output: "apbqrs"
Why: after a-p and b-q, word2 still has "rs" left.

Example 3:
Input: word1 = "abcd", word2 = "pq"
Output: "apbqcd"

Constraints:
1 <= len(word1), len(word2) <= 100
Both words are lowercase English letters.

Write: def merge_alternately(word1, word2) — the driver calls it on word1 = "abc", word2 = "pqr" (case = [word1, word2]) and prints the merged string.

idea.rule: zip stops at the shorter word — whatever's left of the longer one has to be added on.
idea.detail: Walking two inputs together is what problem 167 (Reverse String) did with two pointers; here zip does the pairing: a with p, b with q, c with r. But zip stops the moment the SHORTER word runs out — it never hands you the extra letters. Those leftovers are a slice (like problem 026): after n = the shorter length, word1[n:] + word2[n:] is the tail, and only one of them is non-empty.

watch.code:
def merge_alternately(word1, word2):
    out = ""
    for a, b in zip(word1, word2):
        out += a + b
    n = min(len(word1), len(word2))
    out += word1[n:] + word2[n:]
    return out

word1, word2 = case
print(merge_alternately(word1, word2))

why_line: zip pairs letters only until the shorter word runs out. On "abc"/"pqr" nothing's left over, so the draft looks right — but with "ab"/"pqrs" the "rs" never gets a partner, and zip silently drops it.

explain.rule: zip is a dance that ends when one line runs out of dancers — the extras on the longer line never get onto the floor.
explain.bridge: pairs has 3 pairs here. If word2 were "pqrs", how many pairs would zip make — and where would the 's' go?

fix.rule: Interleave with zip, then add the leftover tail of the longer word: word1[n:] + word2[n:].

walk.gloss: Pair up the letters while both words have one.
